LinuxGSM - Day of Infamy Linux Game Server

notes: Stock Source SDK 2013 dedicated server (srcds -game doi, per LinuxGSM startparameters), so the Valve Source RCON wire protocol on TCP at the game port. RCON has no separate enable cvar: setting rcon_password in doi/cfg/server.cfg turns it on (LinuxGSM's shipped DayOfInfamy/server.cfg sets exactly that), and there is no separate RCON port - it rides the game port, whose cvar is hostport (Source 2013 cvarlist: 'hostport 27015 Host game server port'); the Steam dedicated-server guide states 27015 is 'UDP for traffic, TCP for RCON'. kickid and banid accept either the transient userid from status or the persistent Steam ID; this file moderates by Steam ID (STEAM_x:y:z, the uniqueid column of status) because userid changes on every reconnect. kickid's trailing {reason} is the engine's documented second argument ('Kick a player by userid or uniqueid, with a message'). banid takes MINUTES first, then the id, with an optional trailing 'kick' that drops the player immediately - 0 minutes is a permanent ban. IMPORTANT: banid is in-memory only; the ban is lost on restart unless 'writeid' is also issued, which appends the ban to doi/cfg/banned_user.cfg (the stock server.cfg execs banned_user.cfg and banned_ip.cfg on boot). The schema has no way to chain a second command, so an operator relying on this file's ban must issue writeid separately - this is the main footgun here. Ban-file lines are written unquoted as 'banid <minutes> <STEAM_x:y:z>' (seen as both 'banid 0 STEAM_0:0:...' and float minutes); lineIdPattern tolerates an optional leading quote defensively. removeid unbans live but likewise needs writeid to persist. IP bans use addip/removeip against doi/cfg/banned_ip.cfg and are not modelled here. No motd command exists - the MOTD is the motd.txt file. 'say' is the engine-standard Source broadcast; it is not called out on any Day-of-Infamy-specific page, it is inherited from the engine, as are status/kickid/removeid/writeid. On kick form: the Steam dedicated-server guide lists both 'kick <name>' and 'kickid <id>'; in the Day of Infamy RCON thread an admin ADVISES that a nickname 'might not work for special chars so use SteamID instead' - that is advice, not an observed failure, and the poster's kick/kickid attempts in that same thread were all diagnosed as 'you are not logged in via rcon_password'. kickid with a Steam ID is used here because a name is not a stable identifier, not because plain kick was demonstrated broken. The exact column layout of status was not observed on a live Day of Infamy server; the linePattern tolerates the optional second numeric column some Source builds print before the quoted name. Unverified against a live server.
